s1: Nine in the morning. Walter's phone says it's time for today's check-in.
s2: Some people type. Walter just talks.
s3: The questions are simple. He answers in his own words. The transcript appears right on his phone, and only there.
s4: Names and details are stripped out on the device. Walter reads what would be shared, and he approves it.
s5: Only coded fields leave: symptom, severity, week. No audio. No words. No name. And he gets a receipt.
s6: The company sees patterns, never people. Groups under five are hidden.
s7: His doctor gets a sealed copy only his care team can open. When Walter walks in, the history is already there, and the follow-up questions write themselves.
s9: His doctor has more time to guide him. The company can follow its trial more closely.
s10: SafeSignal. Someone is looking out for you.
